title: Repertoire, reading music and the nine-piece Marable band
summary: With Marable they played ragtime like Maple Leaf Rag from written parts, in a nine-piece band; Foster discusses when tubas arrived and his tuba playing.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: Pops Foster, April 21st, 1957, Rule 3. What kind of music did you play with faith?
Ragtime. Same thing with the called Dick Slater, eh? Maple Leaf Rag.
All by head or were there a...
No, readin'. Oh yeah? Yeah. Readin'. See, I always could read a little bit. Not too much always.

Let me see, we had trombone, two trombones, clarinet, and melaphone. Was it Dave Jones? Yeah, Dave Jones, melaphone, guitar, bass, piano, and drums. Nine pieces. And then people would rave and bother saying...
Were you playing string bass? No, two bass.
No, tuba didn't come out until around 1920 or 20 or 21.
But I hear you used to play tuba.
Well, I played tuba. I didn't buy a tuba until way late. And I heard you were a good tuba player. Well, I don't know. I don't think I'm a good string bass player.
Well, I don't agree with you. Eh? I think you're great.
